This is the water heater issue specific to Chicago's building stock, and the reason a heating company should look at your swap.

In a typical bungalow or two-flat the furnace and the water heater both vent into one masonry chimney sized for the pair. Four things decide whether a whole-system quote is complete. Most quotes cover two of them.

||Balance point, and why it decides your bill::

The balance point is the outdoor temperature at which your heat pump stops being the cheaper way to heat your home. Above it the heat pump runs. Below it the backup takes over. Where that line sits is a setting, and it is the single most consequential number in a Chicago heat pump installation.

Set it too high and you burn gas or strip heat on mild days when the heat pump would have been cheaper. Set it too low and the heat pump grinds away inefficiently in deep cold, or simply cannot keep up.

The right balance point depends on your equipment's rated capacity curve, your building's heat loss, and the current ratio of gas to electricity prices - which moves. It is not a factory default and it should not be left at one.

Ask whoever quotes you where they will set your balance point and why. If the answer is vague, so is the efficiency claim on the quote.
